summary.title: How today's fastest growing B2B businesses found their first ten customers
summary.one_liner: You learn the three growth strategies (personal network, going where customers already are, and press) that about twenty hyper-growth B2B companies, including Figma, Stripe, Slack and Shopify, used to land their first ten customers.
keywords: seek out customers where they are
takeaways: Almost every B2B company's earliest growth comes from three sources: personal network, going to where potential customers spend time, and press.
Start with your own network (friends, former colleagues, investors, incubator peers) and move on once it runs out.
Strong personal networks matter more when you have to sell the product rather than let customers adopt it bottom-up.
Communities such as the Ruby on Rails community, Hacker News, developer forums and Twitter were common channels for early customers.
Getting press is rarely the way to start; the author suggests it works best as a planned launch.
summary.summary: Lenny Rachitsky's newsletter post compiles stories from about twenty B2B startups on how they got their first customers, drawing on interviews, old talks and founder contributions. It organizes the stories into three strategies: tapping personal networks (Slack, Salesforce, Stripe, Gusto), seeking out customers in their communities (Shopify, New Relic, Plaid, Figma, Segment, Dropbox), and getting press (Canva, Twilio, Slack). Each story includes a quoted founder or early employee and a source link where available. A follow-up post for paid subscribers covers how these companies closed their first ten customers.
